previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic systolic heart failure, and atrial fibrillation was admitted with a 5-day history of generalized weakness and 1 day of shortness of breath. He had missed a scheduled blood transfusion and increased fluid intake prior to admission. On evaluation, he showed signs of fluid overload with bilateral pulmonary edema on imaging. He underwent hemodialysis with removal of 4.5 liters of fluid, leading to resolution of dyspnea. He received one unit of packed red blood cells for anemia, with improvement in symptoms. An echocardiogram revealed moderate right ventricular dysfunction and pulmonary hypertension but preserved left ventricular function. He experienced transient atrial flutter with rapid ventricular response after restarting diltiazem, which was managed with a single oral dose. His heart rate stabilized, and he was discharged home in stable condition with home physical therapy, instructions to monitor daily weight, and plans to evaluate for occult gastrointestinal bleeding.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ hx ESRD on HD (___), CHF, afib not anticoagulated,  
presenting with chest pain and BRBPR.  

#BRBPR/anemia: pt with extensive hx of GIB from both upper 
(gastric, duodenal and jejunal AVMs) as well as lower 
(diverticulosis throughout the colon, hemorrhoids). Pt w BRBPR 
and 5pt HCT drop since being discharged ~ 1 week prior on 
aspirin. Anemia was C/b chest pain and elevated cardiac enzymes 
suggestive of demand ischemia. He was hemodynamically stable 
throughout his entire hospitalization. He received 2 units of 
blood with a discharge Hct of 30 and resolution of blood in the 
stool. Endoscopy showed nodular gastritis and an inflammatory 
polyp. Colonoscopy showed a non-bleeding ulcer. The cause of the 
bleed likely in territories unexplored by scopes ie small bowel 
that spontaneously resolved. Follow up needed for bipsy results 
from EGD and colonoscopy. Patient was discharged off of aspirin 
(see NSTEMI below)
 
# NSTEMI: Patient presented with CP in the setting of anemia and 
BRBPR. Cardiology was consulted and believed the CP to be 
atypical and related to demand ischemia, commenting that 
although CK-MB and troponin were elevated to the highest that 
have been recorded for this patient, they were still 
unimpressive given the entire clinical picture. Patient was 
started on nitropaste in house, which alleviated the chest pain. 
Beta blocker was not started because of the patient's history of 
cocaine use. Diltiazem was used for rate control. Initially 
patient was given one dose of baby aspirin for the chest pain. 
Maximum dose simvastatin was also started in this setting. In 
discussion with cardiologist Dr. ___ decision was made to 
start imdur for anginal symptoms. Aspirin was discontinued due 
to GI bleed and also the likely pathophysiology of patient's 
heart disease - microvascular given hx of cocaine use and cath 
in ___ showing clean coronaries. Patient was discharged with 
home diltiazem, imdur, and simvastatin at half (history of 
myalgias and lipid profile). 

# ESRD: Secondary to diabetic nephropathy, continued On HD 
___. Continued home sevelamer, cinecalcet with low 
phos, low K diet  
 
# Atrial fibrillation: continue dilt and digoxin 
 
# DM2: continued on home lantus and HISS
